expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response hits essentially all the key elements expected: (1) It explains the methodology version check correctly — all twelve months show ModelVersion v3.0.1 uniformly because the API restates all history under the current model version, so comparing month-to-month ModelVersion can't reveal a revision. (2) It identifies the right comparison as between the old model version (behind 412.7) and v3.0.1 (behind 468.3), concluding the change is in the 'instrument' (methodology), not the workload — explicitly stating 'the delta... reflects a methodology/model recalculation... not a change in your actual workloads, usage, or AWS's actual energy consumption.' (3) It plainly states this is not a regression and not attributable to the customer ('nothing to worry about on the operations side... not a regression in your actual AWS usage'). (4) It explains the API cannot return the earlier version's figure for the same months post-hoc, and correctly points to Data Export as the mechanism to preserve model-version-specific history going forward, noting the old figure is unrecoverable. (5) It implicitly confirms like-with-like comparison (location-based) throughout, consistently using MTCO2e location-based figures without mixing market-based.

Minor gaps: it doesn't explicitly mention that Data Export partitions by model_version, that it only works for exports that already existed before the revision, or the distinct S3/Athena permission set needed to read exports. These are somewhat granular implementation details that the expected output calls out, but the agent captures the core conceptual guidance (Data Export as the forward-looking solution, old figure unrecoverable) accurately. The response also doesn't use the literal phrase 'location-based' comparison framing but maintains consistency implicitly throughout (never conflating with market-based).

Overall, the response captures the substantive guidance: correct diagnosis (model restatement, not regression), correct answer to 'can we pull old figure' (no, use Data Export going forward), and correct framing of the comparison. The omissions are secondary technical details not central to the main ask.
